title: Week 3 - Software Architecture
content: The fundamental structures of a software system and the discipline of creating such structures. Key elements include: - Components - Connectors - Configuration - Constraints The quality of an architecture can be determined via NFRS that define system behavior beyond just features. These NFRs have trade-offs meaning that improving one may weaken the other. ## Attributes of an Architecture ### Scalability The ability to handle increased load without performance degradation. There are two types: 1. Vertical scaling (scale-up): Increasing the size of an existing instance by increasing memory, CPU, etc. 2. Horizontal scaling (scale-out): Adding more instances We also have: 1. Read scalability: CDN, caching 2. Write scalability: DB partitioning / sharding 3. Elastic scalability: Auto-scaling on cloud ### Performance The speed at which a system processes requests. This includes latency, throughput and load time. It can be optimized via caching, compression, indexing, etc. ### Availability The uptime of a system (measured in 9s). Downtime can happen due to server crashes, DB failures and network outages. ### Maintainability The ease of modifying the system with minimal risk. ### Security Protecting the system from unauthorized access and breaches. ## CAP Theorem There are tradeoffs between the quality attributes of an architecture. The CAP theorem is a good example: CAP: Consistency vs Availability vs Partition Tolerance ## The C4 Model Overview C4 = Context, Container, Component, Code Helps to visualize software at different levels of abstraction. **Context:** How the system fits into the environment **Containers**: The major building blocks of your system **Components**: The modules and components that exist inside a container **Code**: A class diagram ## Monolithic Architecture A single, self-contained application where all functionality is in one tightly integrated codebase. This is deployed and run as one process. Key characteristics: - Tightly coupled components - Shared memory and codebase - Deployed as one unit - Easy to develop early on - Hard to scale selectively Monoliths are deployed as a single artifact and scaling them may require duplicating the whole app. **Pros**: - Ease of development (initially), deployment and testing - Performant because there is no network overhead between modules **Cons**: - Hard to scale specific features - Long build and development times - Barrier to team scaling - Small changes to a single layer or component require a full redeploy. ## Layered Architecture A logical separation of concerns that is often used inside monolithic applications. ### 3 Tier vs N Tier **3 Tier**: Presentation, Logic, Data **N Tier**: Same logic but layers may be deployed separately
